target.title: fix(agents): reject malformed bundle LSP frames when content length is invalid
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where bundle LSP startup could accept a malformed `Content-Length` frame from an LSP server and initialize tools from a response that was not valid LSP framing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundle LSP stdout parser now accepts exactly one case-insensitive `Content-Length` header with a decimal-only value before reading a JSON-RPC body. Malformed or duplicate `Content-Length` headers fail the LSP session at the bundle LSP runtime boundary without changing LSP tool schemas, bundle discovery, process launch, config, or valid lowercase header behavior.

## User Impact

Users with bundle-provided LSP tools no longer get hover, definition, or references tools materialized from malformed LSP frames, while valid LSP servers that use lowercase `content-length` headers continue to initialize normally.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: bundle LSP runtime accepts valid case-insensitive `Content-Length` headers and refuses malformed or duplicate malformed `Content-Length` startup frames before materializing LSP tools.
- Current-head proof at `61bd6699570744d6e11f087db8365f8411e8045f`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts` passed with 15 tests.
- Guard proof: `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` is 596 physical lines, matching the current `upstream/main` baseline for the TS max LOC guard; `.
ode_modules\.bin\oxfmt.cmd --check --threads=1 src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts` passed.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD --model gpt-5.6-terra --thinking low --no-web-search --codex-speed fast` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the focused regressions keep lowercase `content-length` frames working, and malformed suffix or duplicate malformed `Content-Length` frames leave `runtime.sessions` and `runtime.tools` empty while the LSP process is cleaned up.
